### 1. Scene
A breakfast plate with scrambled eggs, bacon, roasted potatoes, and fresh fruit, plus a few cucumber pieces.

### 2. Vessel
A large, roughly square dinner plate. Allowing for its rounded corners, I estimate an effective circular diameter of **26 cm** for the area calculation:  
**3.14 × 13² ≈ 531 cm²**.

### 3. Items
Watermelon, honeydew melon, pineapple, scrambled eggs, bacon, roasted potatoes, and cucumber. No separate sauce or dressing is visible; cooking fat is included in the cooked-food energy estimates.

### 4–7. Area, volume, weight, and energy
Heights represent the average outer envelope of each pile. Bulk density is the only volume-to-weight reduction applied.

| Item | Plate area | Area (cm²) | Height (cm) | Gross volume (ml) | Density (g/ml) | Weight (g) | kcal/100 g | Energy (kcal) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Watermelon | 24% | 127 | 1.6 | 204 | 0.65 | 133 | 30 | 40 |
| Honeydew | 8% | 42 | 1.8 | 76 | 0.65 | 50 | 36 | 18 |
| Pineapple | 9% | 48 | 1.6 | 76 | 0.65 | 50 | 50 | 25 |
| Scrambled eggs | 14% | 74 | 1.0 | 74 | 0.95 | 71 | 160 | 114 |
| Bacon | 13% | 69 | 0.5 | 35 | 0.95 | 33 | 500 | 165 |
| Roasted potatoes | 7% | 37 | 1.6 | 59 | 0.65 | 39 | 160 | 62 |
| Cucumber | 3% | 16 | 1.0 | 16 | 0.65 | 10 | 15 | 2 |

The area shares total **78%**, leaving about 22% of the plate uncovered.

### 8. Sanity check
The estimate is **386 g and approximately 426 kcal**. This is plausible for a fruit-heavy breakfast with a modest portion of eggs, several overlapping bacon strips, and a few potato pieces. Bacon thickness and cooking fat are the largest energy uncertainties.
